description:
Slow tests are refactored, never excused. This brings every test the measurement flagged under its layer's limit.

## Background

The per-test benchmark note under `dev/benchmarks/` lists each test above its layer's limit. Tests that wait on wall-clock timers or sleeps (lease expiry, lock timeouts, server start-up and shutdown, watch loops) are the usual cause. They drive time through an injected clock or an explicit event instead.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every test the benchmark note lists runs under its layer's limit on a quiet host, re-measured with the same method.
- [hard] REQ-02: No refactored test sleeps or waits on wall-clock time to observe the property it owns. Time-dependent behaviour is driven through an injected clock, a channel or an explicit readiness signal.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each refactored test still owns the property it owned before, at the same or a cheaper layer, with no weakened assertion, no ignored test and no test deleted without its property moving to another owning test.

## Decisions

- D-01: REQ-01's quiet-host evidence for the document and lease tests is the host-wide quiet window (loads 1.82, 3.32, 3.94); their code is unchanged since. The serve test, changed afterwards to an injected clock, was re-measured alone under the exclusive lock at loads 3.36, 3.48 and 3.48: median 0.015 s against 2 s. Both are recorded in `dev/benchmarks/per-test-durations-1eb949a5/remeasure-4a01ccba/README.md` (steward ruling, 2026-11-04).

## Notes

If a test cannot meet the limit without losing its property, report it as a blocking concern rather than raising the limit.
title: Refactor every test over the per-test limit
